question: Non-polar molecules possess ______.
solution:
The correct answer is__ **instantaneous dipole moment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Non-polar molecules have an even distribution of electrons across the molecule, resulting in no regions of partial positive or negative charge.
 
• These molecules typically consist of identical atoms or atoms with similar electronegativities, such as in diatomic molecules like N₂ or O₂.
 
• Non-polar molecules do not have a permanent dipole moment, meaning they do not have a net separation of electrical charge.
 
• Even though non-polar molecules have no permanent dipole moment, they can still possess a temporary **"instantaneous dipole moment"** due to the random fluctuations in their electron clouds, which can create a temporary positive and negative charge separation within the molecule. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• Examples of non-polar molecules include noble gases (e.g., He, Ne) and hydrocarbons like methane (CH₄).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronegativity:** It is a measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons. Non-polar bonds occur when atoms have similar electronegativities.
 
• **Polar vs. Non-polar:** Polar molecules have a significant difference in electronegativity between bonded atoms, creating partial charges and a dipole moment. Non-polar molecules do not exhibit these characteristics.
 
• **Van der Waals Forces:** Non-polar molecules primarily interact through Van der Waals forces, which are weaker than the dipole-dipole interactions found in polar molecules.
 
• **Solubility:** Non-polar molecules are generally soluble in non-polar solvents (like oils and fats) but insoluble in polar solvents (like water).
 
• **Instantaneous Dipole:** Although non-polar molecules do not have a permanent dipole moment, they can have instantaneous dipoles due to temporary imbalances in electron distribution, leading to weak London dispersion forces.
